newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND MAKE BOLD START IN CHASE FOR 305.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND MAKE BOLD START IN CHASE FOR 305.

text.p: England were 71 for the loss of one wicket at tea on the fourth day of their third cricket test against New Zealand on Monday, in their quest for 305 to win.
England's senior pairing of captain Mike Atherton, not out on 35, and Alec Stewart on one, may hold the key to England's chase.
Only once - against Australia in 1928/29 -- have England ever managed over 300 in the fourth innings to win.
They began in promising style today with Atherton and Nick Knight weathering the new ball and reaching 64 with few qualms.
But 18-year-old, left-arm spinner Daniel Vettori induced Knight on 29 to loft to mid-on where Heath Davis held the catch.
Vettori, who with an innings of 29 not out in the morning, was instrumental in allowing New Zealand to reach 186 and setting England a challenging target.
Vettori had taken one for nine from six overs, and looms as possibly England's biggest threat in their chase. He was extracting considerable turn out of the bowlers' footmarks.
Stewart had a lucky escape when a ball from Vettori ballooned off his front pad and landed just behind the stumps.
New Zealand had resumed at a precarious 95 for six with Chris Cairns belting a typically belligerent 52 as the other main contributor for the morning.
